column1: 1,1,Introduction to EB-1A,"The EB-1A visa category is reserved for individuals who demonstrate extraordinary ability in sciences, arts, education, business, or athletics. Unlike most employment-based visas, EB-1A does not require a job offer or labor certification — you are self-petitioning based on your achievements alone. To qualify, you must demonstrate sustained national or international acclaim and provide documentation showing that you are one of the small percentage who has risen to the very top of your field. USCIS evaluates your case against the regulatory criteria at 8 CFR 204.5(h)(3). You must meet at least 3 of the 10 criteria, and then demonstrate through a totality of the evidence that you meet the extraordinary ability standard.",1,15,2026-04-17 15:53:13.863567+00

2,1,The 10 Criteria: An Overview,"The 10 criteria cover a broad range of achievements. Not all criteria are equally weighted by USCIS officers in practice. Strong criteria for ML/AI researchers: Scholarly Articles (most important), Judging (peer review is a powerful proxy for peer recognition), Original Contributions (impact metrics matter: citations, downloads, products), Critical Role (demonstrate your position relative to peers). Supporting criteria: Awards (nationally/internationally recognized only), Membership (must require outstanding achievement for admission), Published Material (about you, not by you), High Salary (90th percentile benchmark). Understanding which criteria to lead with is the first strategic decision in building your case.",2,20,2026-04-17 15:53:13.863567+00

3,1,What RFEs Look Like and How to Avoid Them,"A Request for Evidence (RFE) is not a denial — it is USCIS asking for more documentation. However, an RFE adds 3-6 months to your timeline and introduces uncertainty. Common RFE triggers for EB-1A: 1. Citations described without comparison to field averages. 2. Peer review claimed without official documentation from journals. 3. Critical role claimed without organizational hierarchy evidence. 4. Awards described without proof of national/international recognition. 5. Expert letters that are too generic. Each evidence item in your Vault should be evaluated against this list before submission.",3,25,2026-04-17 15:53:13.863567+00

4,1,Building a Coherent Narrative,"USCIS does not just count criteria — officers evaluate whether the totality of evidence demonstrates extraordinary ability. Your evidence items should tell a coherent story. For an ML researcher: the narrative might be that you developed architectures now used at scale across the industry, your work is cited by leading teams, and you have been recognized by the community through peer review invitations and paper awards. Every piece of evidence should reinforce this narrative.",4,20,2026-04-17 15:53:13.863567+00

5,1,Working with Your Attorney,"Pinnacle prepares you to be the most effective client your attorney has ever had. A well-prepared client typically reduces attorney review time by 40-60% and produces a stronger petition. What to bring your attorney: a complete Evidence Vault with every document referenced, a clear narrative connecting your achievements, a readiness assessment showing which criteria are strong, and draft cover letter sections for attorney review. Remember: your attorney gives legal advice. Pinnacle gives coaching to prepare your evidentiary record.",5,20,2026-04-17 15:53:13.863567+00

6,2,Citation Evidence: What Counts,"For EB-1A and EB-2 NIW cases, citations serve as evidence of Original Contributions and Scholarly Articles. Not all citations are equal in USCIS adjudication. Strong citation evidence: Google Scholar citation count with date screenshot, comparison to field average using Semantic Scholar or Scopus field-level data, evidence that citing papers are from distinguished institutions or top venues, self-citation percentage analysis. Avoid citing raw numbers without context — 200 citations is exceptional in some fields but average in high-volume ML subfields.",1,15,2026-04-17 15:53:17.976574+00

7,2,Google Scholar Setup and Documentation,"Your Google Scholar profile is one of the first things USCIS officers verify. Required setup: public profile with institutional email verified, accurate author disambiguation, verified affiliation, complete list of publications. Documentation package: screenshot of profile showing total citations and h-index date-stamped, individual paper citation counts, citation graph showing growth over time, top citing papers list. Take screenshots at three time points: filing date, 6 months prior, 12 months prior.",2,15,2026-04-17 15:53:17.976574+00

8,2,Expert Letter Strategy,"Expert letters from distinguished researchers are the single highest-ROI action you can take for an EB-1A or EB-2 NIW case. Distinguished letter writers: full professors at R1 research universities, senior scientists at top AI labs, IEEE/ACM Fellows who have reviewed your work, industry leaders who have implemented your research. Letter quality criteria: specific knowledge of your work, concrete description of your unique contribution, comparison to others in the field, statement of national/international recognition. Target 4-6 independent expert letters.",3,15,2026-04-17 15:53:17.976574+00
